races.name: Seadell Shops & Holiday Chalets 'Hands And Heels' Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Pleasant Man
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a recent win at 12f on good going and fit off 12 days, but the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) tempers confidence — it maps as a front-runner yet is listed prominent, and trainer Joey Ramsden has had no winners from 10 runners in the last 14 days; visored, which aids focus but doesn't change the tactical picture.

runners_data.name: Hibernate
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's four-year-old has won twice recently at 12f on firm and good and arrives 36 days fresh; a T14 strike rate of 3/13 provides meaningful trainer confidence, and its prominent style is perfectly suited to tracking an uncontested leader before challenging in the straight.

runners_data.name: Currumbin
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with a long break of 82 days and a trainer with no winners from five runners in the last fortnight; recent form has been largely posted over 16f which is considerably further than today's trip, and its best recent finish (3rd over 13f at Sandown) suggests stamina rather than pace will be its weapon — one that may not be triggered by a steady gallop.

runners_data.name: The Ubermensch
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's four-year-old has posted six consecutive placed or near-miss efforts and carries the lightest weight (130lbs), which is an asset; fitted with a tongue-piece, it has a hold-up style and a T14 rate of only 2/24, suggesting it must win on its own merits — a slow pace in a small field does not play to its closing game.

races.paceDynamic: Pleasant Man is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this four-runner field and, with no genuine challenger disputing the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop throughout the 1m3½f trip on good-to-firm ground at Yarmouth. Hibernate also carries a prominent style tag but there is no evidence of aggressive early speed that would pressure Pleasant Man, meaning the pace is likely to be steady rather than searching. With a lone leader operating comfortably in front and the two hold-up horses — Currumbin and The Ubermensch — required to make significant ground from the rear, the shape of this race will be set from the front and is unlikely to change dramatically until the straight. This strongly favours horses able to travel in behind the leader and pick up in the closing stages, giving the edge to prominent types who can track Pleasant Man and pounce, rather than deep closers who will need the pace to be hot enough to expose a tired leader.

scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Pleasant Man sets a steady, uncontested pace and the prominent tracker Hibernate times a smooth challenge inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Pleasant Man sets a steady, uncontested pace and the prominent tracker Hibernate times a smooth challenge inside the final two furlongs.

scenarios.body: If the steady pace is slow enough that Pleasant Man's stamina and race fitness off 12 days gives it an unassailable lead rounding the home turn.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Picks Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens enough in the final quarter-mile to bring the hold-up horses into play from the rear.
scenarios.body: If the pace quickens enough in the final quarter-mile to bring the hold-up horses into play from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Punter's Race
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls to a walk early and the race degenerates into a sprint finish that scrambles all form lines.
scenarios.body: If the field crawls to a walk early and the race degenerates into a sprint finish that scrambles all form lines.

watchPoints.text: Watch Hibernate's early position — if Toby Moore presses up to track Pleasant Man within the first furlong, it secures the race's most advantageous berth and becomes very hard to pass in a steadily-run contest.

Monitor The Ubermensch for a tardy start or wide passage; six days since last run is short and, if it dwells at the gates, the small field will leave it with too much ground to make up against a controlled pace.

Currumbin's 82-day absence and trainer's 0/5 recent form rate are notable; if it fails to settle or travels awkwardly on good-to-firm ground early, it may not have the finishing kick to threaten off such a slow pace.

Check whether the actual going at Yarmouth tightens further toward firm — the going report consistently shows good-to-firm for the 2:39 slot, and if it rides fast, the stamina of Currumbin (bred for softer, longer races) becomes an additional concern.

Pleasant Man's pacemaking role carries a STYLE_FIT flag — if it is reluctant to lead cleanly from the gates, the race could be momentarily leaderless, briefly compressing the field and unsettling the pace dynamic entirely.

races.name: Weatherbys Racing Bank Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Winning Experience With Moulton Racing Handicap

runners_data.name: Great Mates
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner with course form at 8f and two wins at this trip on good-to-good-firm ground; Ghiani and Botti combine in good nick (1/9 T14), and with 13 days since last run they arrive fresh — the uncontested lead is a major asset though the 135lb top weight over a flat mile on fast ground is the key stamina query.

runners_data.name: Sir Edward Lear
runners_data.note: Interesting drop back from 10f-12f trips, where recent form is solid on good ground; Mason Paetel claims 5lb which offsets the weight, and the visor worn is worth noting as it suggests the stable want him sharper — a hold-up type who needs something to happen in front of him, which is uncertain in this moderate-paced contest.

runners_data.name: Kalamunda
runners_data.note: Front-runner/prominent racer who was second on this exact course, trip and going type last time out for Joseph Parr; the trainer's 0/5 strike rate in the T14 window is a negative angle, and the 4th, 4th finishes before that 2nd suggest he can be placed without always winning, but his profile maps neatly onto the likely race shape.

runners_data.name: Tactical Plan
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose best form has come when pace has been honest — the 0/15 strike rate on similar going is a stark statistic; Ed Dunlop is in reasonable form (3/18 T14) and Saffie Osborne adds experience, but this horse needs more gallop than Great Mates is likely to generate to get competitive late.

runners_data.name: Man Of Desert
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose natural position at the rear will be harder to find with several closers in the field — De Sousa takes over and carries conditions-type experience, but the absence of a win from 11 comparable-going runs and the 35-day absence combine to make this a difficult task without a stronger pace to aim at.

runners_data.name: Big Alex Walmsley
runners_data.note: Low-rated closer who will want to settle at the back but is likely to end up in a tight midfield cluster due to the number of hold-up types in this small field; the 0/6 record on similar going and 0 wins from 5 recent runs tell a consistent story, and Mrs Gansera-Leveque's 0/1 T14 window adds no confidence despite De Sousa-class jockey booking.

races.paceDynamic: Great Mates is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure them, Marco Ghiani should be able to dictate a steady, controlled gallop from the front over Yarmouth's flat mile on good-to-firm ground. Kalamunda will want to track prominently and is likely to sit just off Great Mates's shoulder, meaning the first two positions are fairly settled, but the race will be run at a tempo set entirely by the leader's choosing rather than forced upon them. The field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Man Of Desert and Big Alex Walmsley are genuine hold-up horses who will be shuffled into a midfield cluster rather than finding clear space at the back, which complicates their finishing effort. A controlled, front-led pace with a single sustained run from the turn suits horses who can race prominently or produce a well-timed mid-race move; true come-from-behind closers are disadvantaged because the pace will not be strong enough to soften up the front end sufficiently.

scenarios.body: If Great Mates is allowed to dictate a measured gallop and quickens away from the field entering the final two furlongs.

scenarios.body: If Great Mates's early gallop is strong enough to leave them vulnerable late and Kalamunda or a close tracker pounces in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the front end ties up, freeing a closer to come through on the outside.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong and the front end ties up, freeing a closer to come through on the outside.

scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos, Surprise Winner
scenarios.trigger: If bunching occurs through the pack and a horse with a clean passage finds an unexpected gap late.

watchPoints.text: Watch Great Mates at the start — if Ghiani elects to stride on immediately and builds even a three-length lead by halfway, the lack of any pace rival to challenge them makes it very difficult for the hold-up horses to close the gap on fast ground.

Monitor Kalamunda's position in the early stages — if Jack Mitchell allows them to drift back beyond third rather than sitting tight on the leader's quarters, their chance of pegging back Great Mates late on this flat track diminishes sharply.

Man Of Desert and Big Alex Walmsley are true rear-runners compressed into midfield by the race shape; if the pace is moderate and they cannot find clear running room on the home straight, both are vulnerable to simply running out of ground before hitting top gear.

Sir Edward Lear is tackling a distance well short of their recent efforts at 10f-12f — watch whether they travel comfortably through the race or begin to get on their toes early, as a horse used to longer trips over a flat mile can either be freshened or caught out for toe.

races.name: Mark Sumner Handicap

runners_data.name: Give Me The Night
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with the highest sim-going strike rate in the field (2 places from 9 on Good), though wins have eluded him; tongue tie and 29 days since last run are neutral, but trainer Rimell's 0/5 over 14 days is a mild negative — needs a clean run from the rear in what will be a bunched finish.

runners_data.name: Midnight's Dream
runners_data.note: Has the strongest sim-going placed record of any runner here (1 win, 2 places from 15 on comparable ground), which counts for something in a sprint finish; Jack Mitchell's booking is an upgrade, but 11 consecutive blank runs in recent form makes the win elusive and he remains a place contender rather than a banker.

runners_data.name: Mart
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's second string on the day — his natural instinct is to race from behind, and with the field stacked with hold-up types, he is likely to be squeezed for a position; 0 wins and 0 places from 15 sim-going runs makes the profile hard to trust, and a STYLE_FIT of 0.90 tempers confidence significantly.

runners_data.name: Campani
runners_data.note: David Simcock's runner returns after 50 days off and has legitimate Good-ground form (1W4P from 10 sim-going runs), giving him the strongest case of any runner here; Dougie Costello may opt to push forward given there is no natural pace-setter, and if that gambit works, his tactical versatility becomes decisive.

runners_data.name: Luminous Warrior
runners_data.note: The second Cunha runner, another genuine hold-up type who will be competing with stablemate Mart and the rest of the rear-guard for the same patch of ground; tongue tie noted, but 0 wins from 15 sim-going runs and a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 reflect that racing out of his preferred role in this shape is a real concern.

runners_data.name: Shaws Phoenix
runners_data.note: Cheekpieces suggest connections are trying to generate more early energy from a horse that has nevertheless finished placed in 2 of 15 sim-going runs; at OR=48 he carries the joint-lowest weight, which may help in a sprint, but a trainer strike rate of 0/3 over 14 days and some modest form figures dampen expectation.

runners_data.name: Sporty Socks
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old dropping back from 10f trips to a mile — on paper the shorter distance and quicker Good-to-Firm ground could suit better, but 0 wins and 0 places from 8 sim-going appearances tell a sobering story; at OR=46 the weight is light and Kieran O'Neill could find daylight in a compressed finish, though 65 days absence is a query.

races.paceDynamic: With every single runner in this field carrying a hold-up profile, there is no confirmed front-runner and no horse likely to impose a genuine gallop from the outset — the early tempo at Yarmouth over a mile will almost certainly be pedestrian, with runners drifting in a tight bunch before the race ignites in the final two furlongs. The going is Good to Firm (the official report confirms this for the 4:50), which will keep the ground lively and reward horses that can quicken sharply from a compressed field. Campani and Shaws Phoenix both carry headgear flags and have shown they can travel prominently when circumstances demand, making them the likeliest candidates to drift forward and set whatever tempo there is, but neither is a natural front-runner. The race shape heavily favours hold-up horses with a genuine late kick, but the critical caveat is that with all seven runners being true closers, the sprint finish will be a lottery of positioning — those with the highest OR, best sim-going credentials on Good/Good-to-Firm, and cleanest recent form will have the marginal edge in what becomes a dash from two furlongs out.

scenarios.body: If no horse takes a meaningful hold on the race and the field crawls to the home turn before a mass sprint develops.

scenarios.body: If Campani's jockey Dougie Costello decides to press forward from the gate and establish a lone, controlled lead.

scenarios.body: If a slightly stronger early pace develops and the true hold-up horses get a genuine target to aim at in the final furlong.

scenarios.title: Outsider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a crawl and a horse with lower expectations seizes a favourable position uncontested.
scenarios.body: If the race is run at a crawl and a horse with lower expectations seizes a favourable position uncontested.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Dougie Costello pushes Campani forward from the gate — if he does, it transforms the race shape entirely and gives the only horse with controlled-pace credentials a potential free lead.

The entire field is hold-up oriented, meaning stalls positions and early jockey decisions will disproportionately determine who gets a clear run in the sprint — draw and early positioning are critical to monitor.

Mart and Luminous Warrior are stablemates trained by Dylan Cunha racing on the same day; if connections deploy one as a pacemaker, it would create a tactical wrinkle the market may not have priced in.

Good to Firm ground is confirmed for this race — any runner whose recent form came on soft or standard-artificial surfaces (notably Midnight's Dream and Give Me The Night with Soft/Standard heavy histories) should be assessed carefully for going suitability.

Sporty Socks has not run for 65 days and steps down in trip from 10f to 1m; if fitness is sharp, the drop could unlock speed previously unseen, but the absence makes this a significant unknown in a tight, sprint-style finish.

races.name: Branfords Handicap

runners_data.name: Giant
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a placed effort over this course and distance in similar good ground, though his recent form shows more consistency at 8f on Standard; Ryan Kavanagh's 5lb claim is a practical asset in a modest handicap, and his sim-going record of 0W2P flags him as a placer rather than a winner.|

runners_data.name: Wilde And Dandy
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the mount on a horse who boasts a win at 7f on standard — his closest available surface to fast ground — but 147 days off the track raises a significant fitness query; a confirmed rear-of-field operator, his chance depends entirely on others setting a strong enough pace to reel in.|

runners_data.name: Dion Baker
runners_data.note: Arrives in career-best form with three wins from his last four starts at 6-7f on good ground, with the form string 441113 reading as a horse who has found his level; headgear noted, trainer Michael Wigham running at a sharp 4/5 strike rate over 14 days, and only 2 days since last run merits monitoring for fitness but he ran well fresh before. His natural style is hold-up but he has demonstrated the ability to race handily when required.|

runners_data.name: Federal Envoy
runners_data.note: A true rear-of-field type whose sim-going record of just 2 placed efforts from 15 runs on comparable ground is damning; the 14-day gap is manageable and Marco Ghiani is a competent booking, but this horse's 0W1P profile on good-ground equivalents and tendency to race at the back makes him a tough sell in this shape — his redistribution to midfield reflects necessity rather than preference.|

runners_data.name: Dancing With Drums
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race, able to dictate an uncontested lead under Dougie Costello; his trainer Adam Kirby is not in hot form (1/10 over 14 days) and his history shows 0 wins from 3 starts on good ground, but no horse here can take the lead from him, making positional advantage his primary asset regardless.|

runners_data.name: Adelaide Bay
runners_data.note: Has raced consistently at 7f on Standard ground but her best effort — a second — came on that surface, and she has never placed on anything faster; Stevie Donohoe is a capable claimer but the horse's redistribution from her natural trailing position is a concern, and her 28-day absence compounds the risk in a race where she is unlikely to get the pace collapse she needs.|

runners_data.name: Jungle Knight
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old who landed his last win on soft ground at 7f and has yet to prove himself on fast going — the step to Good to Firm is a meaningful query; headgear noted (t), and Mikey Sheehy's record on the horse is unknown, but at OR 60 he is competitive on paper and his lightly-raced profile leaves open the possibility of improvement.|

runners_data.name: Hakin Adraar
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old whose form reads 407-40 and whose sim-going record of 0W0P from 2 runs on comparable ground is uninspiring; Dylan Hogan is an apprentice booking and the trainer's 14-day record of 1/4 is modest — a genuine hold-up type who needs strong pace to emerge, and this race is unlikely to provide it.|

runners_data.name: Mayflower Rock
runners_data.note: The lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 52, flagged as a fader in the finish — a combination that makes her a significant underdog; only three career runs to assess, all on Standard or Good ground at 6f, making this step to 7f a trip query as well. Dylan Cunha's 3/26 trainer strike rate over 14 days offers little compensating angle.|

races.paceDynamic: Dancing With Drums is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 7f handicap at Yarmouth on Good to Firm ground, and with no genuine challenger for the early lead, Dougie Costello can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without being pressured. This is a genuinely pace-light race: the bulk of the field — Dion Baker, Federal Envoy, Hakin Adraar, Adelaide Bay and Mayflower Rock — are all natural hold-up types, while Giant, Wilde And Dandy and Jungle Knight also prefer to race off the pace, meaning Dancing With Drums faces no credible threat to his lead position. A lone front-runner controlling a modest, even tempo over 7f on fast ground at a straight, flat track like Yarmouth creates a classic scenario where the leader dictates every yard and the race becomes a test of stamina and a sustained finish rather than a sharp tactical burst. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours prominent and tracking runners who can sit just off the controlled pace, travel into contention and challenge over the final two furlongs, rather than true deep closers who will be left with too much ground to make up against a front-runner who has never been troubled for position. The field holds more hold-up types than the race can accommodate at the rear — Dion Baker and Federal Envoy are the most likely to push forward and race closer than their natural style, given their recent form and competitive need to be involved.

scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls

scenarios.body: If Dancing With Drums is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a measured, comfortable tempo throughout the 7f.

scenarios.body: If a horse sitting second or third throughout travels well within itself and finds a sustained run to collar Dancing With Drums inside the final furlong.

scenarios.body: If multiple horses push forward unexpectedly to challenge Dancing With Drums, creating a contested, pressured gallop that scrambles the expected race shape.

watchPoints.text: Dancing With Drums and Dion Baker — if Dion Baker pushes forward from his mapped position to sit second early, the entire race shape could compress, setting up a two-horse battle that eliminates the field's hold-up contingent entirely.

Wilde And Dandy — 147 days off the track is the longest layoff in the field; if De Sousa finds him short of peak fitness rounding the final two furlongs, he will stop quickly and mislead any reading of the late pace.

Jungle Knight — headgear and the switch to Good to Firm having only won on soft ground creates a going-suitability flashpoint; if he travels sweetly early he could be prominent, but a negative reaction to the firmer surface would see him drop away tamely.

Federal Envoy — only 14 days since last run and a natural hold-up operator redistributed to midfield; watch the early pace as any acceleration from him toward the front would be a genuine market-mover signal worth noting before the off.

Mayflower Rock — flagged as a fader and unproven at 7f, so her position in running at the 5f marker is a useful pace barometer; if she is still traveling after her natural 6f limit, the pace has been genuinely slow.
